slides.title: From World War II to Rwandan Civil War
slides.cap: Historical connection: Post-colonial division and unresolved refugee crisis
slides.body: The end of European colonial rule left Rwanda with hardened political divisions and large refugee communities. Decades of exclusion and failed return eventually produced invasion, civil war, and genocide.

slides.title: Before the Rwandan Civil War
slides.body:
The Rwandan Patriotic Front, formed largely by Tutsi exiles, invaded Rwanda in 1990 against a government facing political crisis and entrenched ethnic division.

The Conflict Takes Shape: The war concerned refugee return, political power, and the survival of communities targeted by extremist ideology. The opening phase established the political goals, alliances, and military problems that shaped every later campaign.

stats.val: The war concerned refugee return, political power, and the survival of communities targeted by extremist ideology.

slides.title: Second Rwanda War
slides.body:
Second Rwanda War marked an important episode in the Rwandan Civil War. It showed how the conflict's political goals were being translated into military action and placed new pressure on both the battlefield and surrounding communities.

Why This Moment Matters: Second Rwanda War was more than an isolated engagement. It helped define the conflict's direction and exposed the strengths and weaknesses of the opposing sides. The war concerned refugee return, political power, and the survival of communities targeted by extremist ideology.

Consequences: The effects of Second Rwanda War extended beyond its immediate result. The 1994 genocide against the Tutsi and killings of moderate Hutu transformed the war into one of the century's worst human catastrophes. Its place in the wider campaign also influenced later military choices and political calculations.

title: International and Human Dimensions
sub: The wider impact of the Rwandan Civil War

slides.title: International Dimension
slides.body:
Uganda supported the RPF, France backed the Rwandan government, and a weak UN mission struggled to implement the Arusha Accords.

The Human Cost: The 1994 genocide against the Tutsi and killings of moderate Hutu transformed the war into one of the century's worst human catastrophes.

stats.val: Approximately 800,000 people murdered during the genocide, plus war deaths

title: Outcome and Legacy
sub: How the Rwandan Civil War ended and what followed

slides.title: The End of the Rwandan Civil War
slides.body: The RPF captured Kigali and ended the genocide, but mass flight and armed groups in Zaire helped ignite further regional wars.
